checks: No eclipse at 25 of 247 covered epochs where the 0.73078 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 42058853 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in automated TESS photometry data. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 1.31% and an orbital period of 0.7308 days, producing a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 160.5 in the analysis. Pixel-level imaging confirms the eclipse signature with a peak signal-to-noise of 51.7, though the centroid offset of 3.1 arcseconds from the target position warrants consideration. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. While the pipeline's machine-learning model assigned a relatively low likelihood score of 0.10, the photometric data passed all quality checks, providing a solid foundation for further investigation.
